Okay, I've just launched a fresh tmux session named “glint” and captured the initial splash screen. The output shows the stylized ASCII art wordmark for Glint along with the status line indicating the current settings (effort max, safe mode, diagnostics on, etc.). This confirms that the TUI boots correctly and the introductory display renders.

My next goal is to verify that the interactive “/intro” command works as intended. The user (or my own testing plan) wants to see the intro replay, specifically to capture the wordmark during its shimmer phase. I need to send the command into the running Glint process inside the tmux session, wait for the animation to complete, then capture the final lines of the pane to inspect the output.

Since the tmux session is already alive (the previous command left it running), I can use `tmux send-keys` to type the command `/intro` followed by Enter. A short pause after sending the keys (≈0.2 s) ensures the command is registered before the Enter keystroke. After that, I should allow a few seconds (about 4.2 s) for the intro animation and shimmer effect to finish; this mirrors the timing I used earlier when capturing the initial splash.

Finally, I’ll capture the pane contents, strip empty lines, and take the last few lines (tail -4) which should contain the completed wordmark and any concluding status line. This will give me a concise snapshot to verify that the intro replay behaves exactly like the first launch.

All of this can be done in a single Bash tool call, targeting the existing “glint” tmux session. The command will be:

```
tmux send-keys -t glint '/intro' && sleep 0.2 && tmux send-keys -t glint Enter && sleep 4.2 && tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -v '^\s*$' | tail -4
```

The description will note that I’m replaying the intro to capture the wordmark with its shimmer phase. This should give me the evidence I need before I move on to any further UI tweaks or documentation updates.
